title: WPPIL/69/2016 of Mohan Chandra Paladiya Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Delay Condonation Application in C.A. No. 6694 of 2017
Miscellaneous Application with R.A. No. 5686 of 2017
In
Writ Petition (PIL) No. 69 of 2016
Mohan Chandra Paladiya .......... Petitioner

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .......... Respondents
Mr. M.S. Pal, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Zaheen, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. S.S. Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent
nos. 1 to 3.
Dated : 07th December, 2017

Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
Delay in filing counter affidavit on behalf of respondent no. 3 is
condoned. Counter affidavit is taken on record. Delay condonation
application is allowed.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed on behalf of the petitioner is taken on record.
Miscellaneous application made therefor stands disposed of.
3. Petitioner has approached this Court seeking the following reliefs:
"i) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents not to divert the
proposed road and survey the road "District Nainital,
Village Baanana- Vadhoda- Gangaliya Gaon for
constructed 04 km. road to Chhoar Kapri road about
1.500 km." according modifying G.O. which is
(Annexure No. 2 to the writ petition).
 ii) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to give the effect
the modified G.O. dated 3.03.2016.
4. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as follows:

2
 That all the villagers of the area passed the Resolution regarding the
road, namely, District Nainital, Village Baanana- Vadhoda- Gangaliya
Gaon. Annexure No. 6 is the recommendation. The respondent no. 3
surveyed the road in the year 2006. The Government Order dated
03.03.2016 came to be modified. Annexure No. 2 was issued to construct
the road along with the budget; but the respondent no. 3 is not surveying
according to the modified Government Order and is diverting the said road
according to their choice to some other direction. It is causing prejudice.
The petitioner filed Annexure No. 8 and is before us.
5. Counter affidavit has been filed in the matter. Therein, it is, inter alia,
stated as follows:
"6. That in reply to the contents of para 3 to 7 of the writ petition it
is submitted that on the consent of the villagers, Gram Pradhan
and the local M.L.A., the construction of a link road from
Government Inter College Bannana in the Legislative
Assembly area, Dhari, to Government Hospital Bannana was
sanctioned vide Government Order dated 16.10.2016 of 2 Km.
length with a cost of Rs. 25.20 lacs in the year 20.10.2011. It is
stated that apart from the aforesaid a sum of Rs. 0.84 lacs was
sanctioned fur the survey of 1.5 Km. long road from Km. 4 of
Baanana Vadhodha-Gangaliya Gaon road to Chhoar Kpari,
vide letter dated 30.08.2011 of the District Magistrate Nainital,
in the District Plan of the year 2011-12. It is, however,
submitted that there was forest land/ Nap land in the alignment
of both the aforesaid roads and there being no consent between
the villagers for either of the alignment, the final alignment of
both the roads could not be done and the proceedings were
hence stalled. It is relevant to state here that now the villagers,
Gram Pradhan and the local M.L.A. have resolved and
requested for the construction of the road from Km. 4 of
Baanana Vadhoda-Gangaliya to Chhoar Kapri instead of the
link road from the Government Inter College Baanana to
Government Hospital Baanana sanctioned under the State plan.
In view of the aforesaid the office of the answering respondent
sent a proposal and the State Government vide its order dated
03.03.2016 sanctioned the aforesaid scheme for construction of
the road from Km. 4 of Baanana Vadhoda- Gangaliya Gaon to
Chhoar Kapri and a sum of Rs. 25.20 lacs have been
sanctioned for the construction of 1.5 Km's length of the
aforesaid road at its first stage. It is submitted that pursuant to
the aforesaid a general meeting was called on 28.04.2016 for
deciding the alignment in which most of the villagers wanted
the construction of the aforesaid road via Gram Baanana,

3
however, the petitioner in the instant writ petition is praying
for the alignment of the aforesaid road via the Gangnath
Temple.
7. That pursuant to the aforesaid situation the department has
completed the survey of both the aforesaid alignment and in
the alignment agree to by most of the villagers, via Gram
Baanana, the proposed length of the road comes to about 0.950
Km's which comprises mostly of private agricultural fields on
which the villagers have been their consent to use them for the
construction of the road. It is submitted that on the other hand
in the alignment proposed by the petitioner the total length of
the road would be about 1.050 km's and most part of the
alignment passes through the forest land.
8. That it is also submitted that in both the aforesaid alignment
some part of the Hills seems to be affected by landslides, on
which Geologist was called for site inspection on 17.04.2016
upon which a report of the Geologist has been submitted on
25.01.2017. It is pertinent to submit here that in the aforesaid
geological report the alignment from Km.4 of Baanana
Vadhoda-Gangaliya Gaon to Chhoar Kapri via village has been
said to be more viable both environmentally and financially. A
copy of report of the Geologist is being filed herewith and
marked as Annexure C.A.-1. Hence, the department is
proceeding to construct the road on the aforesaid alignment as
early as possible. It is submitted that pursuant to the sanction in
the first stage the survey and process of granting compensation
to the villagers is under progress."
6. Rejoinder affidavit has also been filed. We have also set out the case
of the Government.
7. After hearing Mr. M.S. Pal, learned senior counsel for the petitioner
and Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent nos. 1 to 3 and having regard to the nature of the
jurisdiction, we would think that no orders are required in this writ petition.
8. Accordingly, the writ petition is closed.
